The posts here are not independent notes. They form two threads that started
separately and now cross: one on **optimising against two objectives at once**,
one on **what unlearning is and how it should be measured**. This page is the
map — what each post establishes, what it leaves open, and where a later post
corrects an earlier one.

If you are arriving cold and want a single self-contained post, read
[Classical certified unlearning as a privacy metric compares the wrong two
things](posts/2026-08-03-unlearning-aware-dp/): it depends on nothing else here.

## Thread A — two tasks, one step

Given two gradients that disagree, which coordinates of the update deserve to be
trusted, and can the answer be certified rather than assumed? The thread runs
from a hard combinatorial construction to a probabilistic one, then folds them
together, then repairs the noise model underneath.

| # | Post | What it settles | What it leaves open |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | [Gradient masking for two-task alignment](posts/2026-07-23-l1-gradient-masking/) | Feasibility is two linear inequalities in the mask; an $\mathcal{O}(d\log d)$ greedy, **optimal exactly when the active branch never switches**, with a $d=3$ counterexample showing the condition is necessary | Exact algorithm (Q1); the objection that sparsity is the wrong quantity; reweighting as a closed-form baseline |
| A2 | [Adam2D: a calibrated agreement gate](posts/2026-08-03-two-dimensional-adam/) | Adam's step is an uncalibrated probability statement; making it explicit gives a per-coordinate gate $f$ that composes with any aggregation and needs no extra gradient | Correlated measurement noise (Q1); $n>2$ tasks (Q2); per-layer priors (Q3) |
| A3 | [Certifying a two-task step](posts/2026-08-04-certifying-two-task-steps/) | Three levels of guarantee, only one of which uses a prior; the greedy of A1 transports to the gate of A2 exactly; a Pareto-layer reduction and a solver-free optimality certificate | Whether the Lagrangian sweep stays optimal outside this regime (Q1); choosing $\tau_{\mathrm{rel}}$ (Q2) |
| A4 | [Two losses, one batch](posts/2026-08-05-correlated-batch-noise/) | The independence assumption of A2 fails whenever the two losses share a batch, and the correlation is large in practice; the gate becomes an orthant probability, estimable for nothing | see that post's open questions |

**Where they meet.** A1 and A2 turn out to be the same quadratic seen twice: the
violation functional $V$ is identical, with A1's binary mask $m$ replaced by A2's
continuous gate $f$. A3 is the consequence — the gate's feasibility is a
*deterministic* property of the batch, and when it fails A1's greedy repairs it
with the focus weight factoring straight out of the score. A4 then goes back
under A2 and replaces the noise model, which A3 absorbs without changing a line,
because its certificate reads $f$ as an opaque non-negative weight.

## Thread B — what is being measured

| # | Post | What it settles | What it leaves open |
|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | [Classical certified unlearning compares the wrong two things](posts/2026-08-03-unlearning-aware-dp/) | The retraining reference differs from the release by a *procedure*, not only by a record; rectifying it forces an unlearning-aware data space, and prices status confidentiality against retain privacy | Adaptivity and republication; whether confidentiality is the right notion at all |
| B2 | [Doubling the label space](posts/2026-08-03-doubling-the-label-space/) | One softmax over $2C$ cells makes a known binary attribute readable as a direction; $\Delta M$ is exactly a pointwise mutual information, and its sign test costs one pass | The accuracy-versus-$C$ curve; behaviour beyond the Gaussian instantiation |

B1 is about the *definition* one is certifying against; B2 is about *reading a
concept off a model* once the forget/retain status is treated as part of the
label rather than as metadata. They share the move that makes the whole thing
work: promoting the retain/forget tag from an annotation to a typed coordinate of
the data.

**Where the threads cross.** The unlearning-aware data space of B1 and the
doubled label space of B2 are the same augmentation
$\tilde{\mathcal Z} = \mathcal X \times \mathcal Y \times \{\mathsf r, \mathsf f\}$,
used for two different purposes — one to state a privacy condition, one to
extract a direction. And Thread A exists because unlearning is the two-task
problem where the two gradients conflict *by construction* rather than by
accident.

## Corrections log

A journal that never contradicts itself is not being written honestly. What has
been overturned so far, newest first:

| Where | What was claimed | What replaced it |
|---|---|---|
| A3, bi-constrained section | "The Lagrangian sweep is optimal only $47\%$ of the time, median gap 1, max 176" | An artefact of a *wrong* MILP solve. An exact-rational weak-duality certificate proves the sweep optimal on **39/39** well-posed instances |
| A3 vs A2 | A2 presented the batch certificate as inheriting the prior's calibration problems | Only level (ii) depends on the prior; levels (i) and (iii) do not |
| A2, calibration section | The tempting headline "the posterior is calibrated, Adam is not" | Both are badly calibrated; a flat prior is *worse* than Adam at low SNR. What the probabilistic reading buys is diagnosability, not correctness |
| A2, trust region | The $\lVert m \rVert_0$ bound of the source paper | Vacuous for a continuous gate ($\lVert f \rVert_0 = d$ a.s.); restated with the same norm on both sides |
| A1, optimality | "Each removal is the steepest available", presented as optimality | Local descent, not global optimality — and false as stated, since $\tilde s_i$ is the slope of one branch, not of $V = \max(V_A, V_B)$ |
| A1, algorithm | A greedy without the dominance restriction or the $\tilde s_i \ge 0$ exit | Both guards added; without them the loop reports `FAIL` on feasible instances |

Two open questions have since been answered by a later post rather than by me
sitting down to answer them: A2's Q1 (correlated noise) by A4, and A1's Q1
partially by A3 — the *practical* ceiling is a per-instance dual certificate
costing $\mathcal{O}(d)$, while the complexity question is still open.

## What is not here yet

- A real multi-task benchmark for the gate of A2, against a tuned CAGrad. Every
  empirical claim in Thread A currently lives on one small problem — an MLP of
  $8{,}970$ parameters on `digits` — so the setting bias is shared, not just the
  sample size.
- The unlearning-specific evaluation (rUA, MIA) of the certified variant of A3.
- An experiment for B2 at a $C$ large enough for the capacity argument to bite.
